chunks: And among what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Muskan, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who performed tayammum and prayed, then reached water before the time had ended. He said: There is no repetition of the salat (prayer) upon him.

The proper way regarding these reports is that we take his statement, “before the end of the time,” as referring to the state of the salat (prayer), not to the finding of water; because the time of tayammum is the end of the time, as we mentioned in our major book, and reports have also already preceded indicating that.

So the intended sense in the first report would be: if he comes upon water after he has prayed with tayammum within its time; and in the second report: concerning a man who performed tayammum and prayed while he was within time, then afterward found water; and it is understood as involving advancement and delay in wording.

And likewise the third report, his statement: he does not find water, then prays while some of the time still remains for him, then afterward comes to water. And likewise the fourth report, his statement: concerning a man who performed tayammum and prayed before the end of the time, then reached water. If this construction is permissible in these reports, then it does not conflict with what we have mentioned, and all the reports remain sound together.

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ الصَّلَاةِ: repetition of the salat (prayer) after it has already been performed
key_terms.التَّقْدِيرُ: the inferred construction or understood wording needed to reconcile the reports
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the transmitted reports being compared and reconciled
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, whose availability affects the validity of tayammum
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum, the dry ablution in the absence of water
key_terms.خُرُوجِ الْوَقْتِ: the ending of the prescribed prayer time
key_terms.وَقْتَ التَّيَمُّمِ: the operative time in which tayammum is resorted to

ai.seo_question: If someone prays with tayammum and then finds water before the prayer time ends, must the salat (prayer) be repeated?
ai.summary: This passage states that a person who performs tayammum and offers salat (prayer), then later finds water before the prayer time ends, is not required to repeat the prayer. It also explains how seemingly different reports are to be reconciled by understanding the timing expressions as referring to the prayer having been performed within its valid circumstance of tayammum.
